notes.decision: ⲥⲁϣϩ rendered 'seven' per glossary attestation (Lyc. for ⲥⲁϣϥ̄). The 'seven pillars that stand fast' fits the cosmological inventory of cosmic supports — possibly the seven cosmic Pillars/Omophoroi paralleling the seven firmaments.

'this other five gods' = the Five Sons of the Living Spirit (cosmic architects), distinguished from a prior set of five gods (likely the Five Sons of First Man). The doubled five-god schema is standard in Manichaean cosmogony. ⲛⲩϩⲣⲉ ⲙⲡⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'food of the man' likely refers to the cosmic Living Soul that nourishes the macrocosmic Anthropos.
'the cosmos stands fast' — using ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗ idiom (glossary). The 3pl-flavored suffix ⲁⲣⲉⲧⲩ̈ may reflect the cosmos as a plural-of-firmaments construction or be a Lycopolitan dialectal feature.

ⲡⲁⲁⲁⲙⲁⲥ (with double ⲁ) = ⲡⲁⲇⲁⲙⲁⲥ 'the Adamas of Light' — the cosmic warrior-figure who battles the dragons/abortions (cf. accumulated ⲡⲙⲁⲛⲣ̄ⲡⲁⲓⲥ 'the place of battle'). The triple-ⲁ orthography is Lycopolitan/scribal.

Feminine ordinal 'third' (cf. accumulated ⲧⲙⲁϩϣⲁⲙⲧⲉ in glossary) referring back to an implied feminine antecedent — likely a 'greatness' (ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄) or 'kind' (ⲧⲁⲓⲉ). The ⲧ̄- with overline marks the article; ϩⲱⲱⲥ 'likewise/also' is standard Coptic.
'twelve powers' — ⲛⲟⲁⲙ as plural of ⲟⲁⲙ 'power' (per glossary). The twelve powers below match the standard Manichaean cosmology of twelve zodiacal/aeonic powers in the lower hemisphere.
'the count/reckoning of the twelve likenesses' — ⲧⲏⲡⲉ from ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon'; ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ rendered 'likeness' per terminology guide. The twelve likenesses likely correspond to the twelve zodiacal forms.
'the three great pillars of strength' — ⲙⲛⲧⲭⲱⲣⲉ = abstract 'strength' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲧⲭⲱⲣⲉ̄ 'the Strong One/Mighty'). The three great pillars likely refer to a triadic cosmic-supporting structure.

ⲡⲥⲉ retained transliterated as 'the Pse' due to lexical uncertainty. Pairing with ⲡϩⲁⲙⲏⲛ ('the Amen') in a chapter title suggests a liturgical-formulaic element — possibly a salutation, blessing, or cup-related liturgical term, but no secure identification is possible without parallels.
'Tell me, my Lord' — ⲁⲭⲓⲥ = ⲁϫⲓⲥ imperative 'say it' with Lyc ⲭ for ϫ; ⲡⲁⲭⲁⲓ̈ⲥ 'my Lord' (Lyc. for ⲡⲁϫⲟⲉⲓⲥ, cf. ⲡⲁⲭⲁⲓ̈ⲥ in glossary). Standard Kephalaia disciple-petition formula.
